newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher but off week's highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher but off week's highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended higher again Thursday on moderate volume, but the two nearby contracts traded inside Wednesday's range, after the spot May contract climbed to new contract highs yesterday.

"Sentiment is still bullish, after the Green Coffee Association (GCA) stocks data impacted Wednesday, but there was no follow-through buying today and volumes were lower," Refco New York analyst Anne Prendergast said.

"The GCA stocks are only voluntarily reported warehouse stocks and don't include roaster stocks, so we suspect inventories may be higher, given the surge in Latin American exports in recent months," she said.

CSCE coffee prices jumped Wednesday after the monthly report from the New York Green Coffee Association showed supplies of green coffee in U.S. warehouses rose in March by 111,000 60-kg bags to 1,657,000 bags, a smaller rise than expected.
CSCE May coffee ended up 1.75 cents a pound at 209.80 cents Thursday, after trading a 206.10-211.50 intraday range.
But the May contract is approaching first notice day on April 22, while the July contract now has more open interest.
CSCE July coffee ended up 2.20 cents at 187.50 cents, after trading a 185.00-188.50 range.
The May/July backwardation slipped to 22.25 cents from 22.75 cents.
LCE May robusta coffee ended little changed.

Daily momentum oscillators still look very positive, analysts said. But a standard five day slow stochastic indicator has reached overbought levels above 80 percent again, a level from which downward price corrections occurred in early March and early April.

Volatility levels have stopped expanding also, with standard 14-day average true range around 6.35 cents a day and 20-day historical volatility has slipped to around 62 percent from a high around 72 percent in late March and early April.
Other news buoying bullish sentiment this week included a strike by stevedores in at the key Brazilian port of Santos which was set to spread to Rio de Janeiro and Vitoria early Thursday.
Of the 1.53 million bags of coffee shipped from Brazil during March, 1.15 million were shipped from Santos.
But a threatened Colombian truck drivers' strike set for April 20 may be declared illegal by the government, the Colombian Transportation Minister said Thursday.
Coffee prices have surged to their highest levels since 1994 this season, but any relief from higher coffee prices may prove shortlived, analysts said.

Heavy shipments from Latin American origins in the past quarter are likely to abate in the next month as reserves of fresh coffee and stocks are depleted and the 1996/97 harvests wind down, leaving supplies tight again in the summer.
